about.title: Brisbane Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Brisbane is a small city, but its residents drive, shop, and work like anyone in a busy corner of San Mateo County, tucked against US-101 and the Bayshore. That means everyday products — vehicle parts, tools, appliances, children's items, medical devices — pass through this community constantly, and sometimes those products fail. When a defect in design, manufacturing, or warning causes an injury, California law generally lets the injured person pursue the manufacturer, distributor, or retailer under strict liability, without having to prove anyone was careless. That's a meaningful difference from other injury claims, but it still requires preserving evidence and understanding who in the supply chain may be responsible. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result — we simply connect Brisbane residents, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can review what happened and explain the options, on a no-fee-unless-you-recover basis.

whyChoose.title: Why Brisbane Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the product was defective and caused your injury. An attorney can help identify which type of defect applies to your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product. A connected attorney can help sort out who was involved in getting that product into your hands.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Matters Early
items.desc: Keeping the product itself, along with packaging and receipts, can be critical to a strict liability claim. We connect you quickly so an attorney can advise on preserving what you have before it's lost or discarded.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving negligence. An independent attorney can review your situation to determine which legal theory fits best.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging, instructions, or parts. Don't repair or discard it, since it may serve as key evidence. An attorney can advise you on safe storage and next steps.

We connect you with an attorney familiar with California law who can address your specific circumstances.
